title: Horizon-Aware Slew & Capacity-Bucket Controller for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Introduce a new autoscaling policy engine component (HASC - Horizon-Aware Slew Controller) for Dedicated capacity that blends short-horizon predictive demand estimates, per-tenant capacity buckets, and explicit slew-rate limits to provide tighter throughput guarantees while bounding cost and avoiding oscillation.

Why this is needed:
- Existing heuristic and PID-style autoscalers either react too late for rapid request bursts or oscillate when mixed-tenancy contention occurs.
- Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect deterministic throughput windows and predictable cost; we need an autoscaler that enforces both hard safety fences and soft predictive headroom.

High-level approach:
1) Demand Estimator: lightweight quantile estimator (e.g., 95th/99th arrival rate over short windows + exponential smoothing) to predict near-term load horizon (30s-5m).
2) Capacity Buckets: allocate capacity budget per tenant as time-bucketed credits (burst bucket + steady bucket). Buckets decay and refill based on SLA tier and historical utilization.
3) Slew Limiter: cap scale-up and scale-down rates across the fleet and per-tenant to avoid churn; configurable in units of GPUs/replicas per minute and percentage of current fleet.
4) Safety Envelope: enforce min/max fleet sizes, emergency reserve (N spare GPUs per region), and instant fallback rules to compatible model variants when headroom exhausted.
5) Cost-Aware Penalty: when cost target is breached, prefer slower scale-up and tighter burst admission rather than immediate capacity increase.

Algorithm outline:
- On each decision tick (configurable, default 10s):
  * Collect metrics: per-tenant qps, tail latency (p95/p99), queue length, KV cache hit rate, average tokens/sec.
  * Predict demand over horizon H using quantile estimator and trend delta.
  * Compute required replicas R_req = ceil(predicted_tokens_per_sec / capacity_per_replica) with headroom factor based on SLA tier.
  * Clamp R_req by capacity buckets (can't consume more burst credits than available without penalty).
  * Apply slew limiter to generate R_target = clamp(R_current +/- slew_delta, R_req_lowerbound, R_req_upperbound).
  * Validate R_target against Safety Envelope; if violation -> trigger mitigation (prioritize high-SLA tenants, initiate rebalancing, or activate graceful degradation).

Acceptance Criteria:
- The controller produces stable scaling decisions under 3 synthetic workloads: single-tenant burst, mixed-tenancy harmonic traffic, and step-increasing traffic.
- Under burst tests, 95% of requests should see latency < SLO with no more than 2x usual cost increase during the burst window.
- No scale oscillation (>= 3 scale-up/down cycles in 10 minutes) in any test scenario.
- Per-tenant capacity bucket accounting is visible in Console and traceable to costs.

Telemetry & Observability requirements:
- Decision tick events with inputs (predicted demand, R_req, bucket balance, slew_delta) as structured logs.
- Dashboard: per-fleet and per-tenant: current replicas, predicted load, bucket balance, recent scale actions.
- Alert: unmet headroom for > 30s, safety-envelope breach attempt, frequent slew-clamping.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy HASC to one Dedicated cluster in staging with synthetic workloads and manual overrides (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (soft production): enable for low-traffic tenants on a single prod region with monitoring and auto rollback (4 weeks).
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand by SLA tier and region; default off for platinum until validated.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- HASC publishes recommended target replica counts but supports a passive mode (recommendation-only) for 2 weeks before active enforcement.
- Migrate tenant bucketing by importing historical usage for first 24-72 hours to seed buckets.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for estimator and bucket accounting.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with runtime under traffic replay harness (include KV cache cold/warm states).
- Chaos tests: sudden node failures and region outages to validate safety envelope fallback.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Horizon length tradeoff (short horizon = reactive, long horizon = smoother but less precise). Recommend default 60s with configurable upper bound.
- Bucket sizing policy: static vs adaptive. Start with adaptive based on rolling 7-day usage percentile.
- Complexity of estimator: want simple and explainable (quantile+EWMA) vs ML model (better accuracy but higher ops cost).

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/hasc-design
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/248
- Traffic replay harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-replay/tree/hasc-harness
acceptance_criteria: Stable decisions across single-tenant burst, mixed-tenancy harmonic, and step-increase tests
95% of requests meet latency SLO during burst windows with cost increase capped (<=2x)
No scale oscillation exceeding 3 cycles in any 10-minute window
Per-tenant capacity bucket balances are reported in Console and mapped to cost lines
tasks: Add capacity-bucket accounting store and API (ENG-53109.2)
Integrate slew limiter into scaler loop (ENG-53109.3)
Safety envelope enforcement and emergency fallback hooks (ENG-53109.4)
End-to-end tests in staging with traffic replay (ENG-53109.6)
decisions: Use short-horizon quantile estimator + EWMA for trend smoothing (chosen for interpretability)
Bucket refill rules will be adaptive by default and seeded from 7-day percentiles
Default slew-rate limits: max +2 replicas per minute or +20% of fleet per 5 min, whichever smaller
Cost-aware penalties will reduce burst admission before initiating cross-region scaling
telemetry: decision_tick:{timestamp, tenant, predicted_qps, predicted_tokens, R_req, bucket_balance, slew_applied}
scale_action:{timestamp, region, previous_replicas, new_replicas, reason, forced_by}
